decision_description: Two Phase 7 budget gate artifacts for run msca-pf-syn-01 present apparently contradictory gate declarations: (Artifact A) docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json records gate_pass_declaration 'fail', citing BLOCKING-01 — absent lump-sum budget response in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/, and declaring this a blocking gate failure per CLAUDE.md §8.4 and §13.4; (Artifact B) docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json records gate_pass_declaration 'pass' via internal deterministic unit-cost derivation (confirmed_months × published_rates × host_country_coefficient), with all four line items at Confirmed status, unresolved_components empty, and blocking_inconsistencies empty. Conflict: Tier 4 artifact A (lump-sum channel, fail) versus Tier 4 artifact B (unit-cost channel, pass) for the same run and the same gate. Resolution: CLAUDE.md §8.1 as amended by Constitutional Amendment Record C1 establishes an instrument-conditional budget gate rule. MSCA-PF is a unit-cost instrument (confirmed in docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding/selected_call.json and in unit_cost_budget.json instrument_type field). For unit-cost instruments, the budget gate is satisfied by the internal deterministic derivation, not by an external lump-sum response. Artifact A (budget_gate_assessment.json) correctly evaluates the lump-sum integration channel and correctly records a fail — the lump-sum channel is inapplicable to a unit-cost instrument. Artifact B (unit_cost_budget.json) is the authoritative gate artifact for this instrument type, and it passes. The governing artifact for gate_09 evaluation is unit_cost_budget.json; the budget gate passes for run msca-pf-syn-01.
alternatives_considered: Treat both Tier 4 artifacts as equally authoritative and declare the gate unresolved pending operator adjudication — rejected because CLAUDE.md §8.1 (C1) supplies an unambiguous instrument-conditional rule that resolves which budget path governs; the conflict is deterministic, not a judgment call requiring operator input.

Treat budget_gate_assessment.json (fail) as the definitive gate outcome and propagate HARD_BLOCK to Phase 8 — rejected because budget_gate_assessment.json evaluates the lump-sum integration channel, which is constitutionally inapplicable to unit-cost instruments per CLAUDE.md §8.1 (C1); applying the lump-sum gate failure to an MSCA-PF action would violate the instrument-conditional rule and would incorrectly block a validly gated workflow.

Re-run Phase 7 producing a single unified budget gate artifact combining both instrument-path checks — noted as a future orchestration improvement to eliminate dual-artifact ambiguity; not required to resolve the current run because §8.1 (C1) provides unambiguous resolution authority and unit_cost_budget.json is already present and complete.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.1 (Constitutional Amendment Record C1: instrument-conditional budget gate) — for unit-cost instruments (e.g. MSCA-PF), the budget gate is satisfied by the internal deterministic derivation (confirmed_months × published_rates × host_country_coefficient), validated by a byte-equal replay check; the lump-sum external integration channel (budget_gate_assessment.json) is inapplicable to this instrument type and its fail declaration does not constitute a gate failure for MSCA-PF. Supporting: CLAUDE.md §8.4 (C1) — the categorical Phase 8 block is lifted when every budget component resolves to Confirmed or operator-declared Assumed; this condition is met in unit_cost_budget.json. Tier 3 source: docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding/selected_call.json (confirms instrument_type MSCA-PF). Tier 4 source: docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json (provides the passing deterministic derivation; all components Confirmed or Assumed; gate_pass_declaration pass).
rationale: MSCA-PF is a unit-cost instrument. CLAUDE.md §8.1, as amended by C1, establishes that for unit-cost instruments the budget is computed internally by deterministic derivation from published unit costs and that this derivation is not an estimate — it carries no judgment, and determinism supplies the anti-fabrication guarantee that externalisation supplies for lump-sum instruments. The unit_cost_budget.json artifact is complete: formula confirmed_months (24, operator-declared Assumed) × published_rates (Tier 2B docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/unit_cost_rates.json) × host_country_coefficient (78.7% for HU, operator-declared Assumed). All four line items — living_allowance (€119,938.80), mobility_allowance (€17,040.00), research_training_networking (€24,000.00), management_and_indirect (€15,600.00) — resolve to Confirmed status. unresolved_components is an empty array. blocking_inconsistencies is an empty array. Total €176,578.80. Per CLAUDE.md §8.4 (C1), the categorical Phase 8 block is lifted when every budget component resolves to Confirmed or operator-declared Assumed; both operator-declared Assumed components (confirmed_months, host_country) are present with declared sources in docs/tier3_project_instantiation/working_assumptions.json. The budget_gate_assessment.json fail is the constitutionally correct output of the lump-sum validation branch evaluated in isolation; it is not a gate failure for this instrument type. CLAUDE.md §8.1 (C1) unambiguously resolves the conflict: for MSCA-PF, unit_cost_budget.json governs gate_09 evaluation. The budget gate passes for run msca-pf-syn-01. No further operator intervention is required.
